item.text: {"piece_id":"01","title":"CAD Agents Move Into the Draft-and-Check Loop","question":"What changed, and which developments matter most to this audience?","argument":"Frontier models are becoming useful for creating and finding editable CAD artifacts, but the practical advance is a faster draft-and-check loop rather than autonomous engineering. An independent hands-on test found two selected drawing-to-CAD outputs passed a mass check, while a broader research record reports benchmark gains but no physical-part tests of tolerances or manufacturability. The change for engineering leaders is that agents can produce more reviewable geometry, making verification and approval more consequential.","synthesis":"Engineering.com supplies a concrete mass-validation check on selected STEP outputs; the MIT-CDFG survey puts that narrow result beside a wider record of parametric-CAD benchmarks and missing engineering checks. Cadalyst shows vendors extending automation across lifecycle workflows, while the podcast’s simulated robotics results reinforce that executable task checks do not establish dependable physical operation. Together, these sources support treating agents as constrained producers of artifacts that require domain-specific verification.","limitations":"The independent CAD check covers only two practice drawings and mass after STEP import; it does not establish dimensional accuracy, tolerances, feature-history fidelity, manufacturability, or performance on production drawings. Autodesk’s demonstration establishes what was shown, not production reliability, and the robotics result is based on simulation and a single run per
